cells.tense: You are here with your hands on it, giving the work what it needs at the speed it can take.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've been tending to the person it will outlast — say out loud what it was for, and let their thanks land without waving it off.
cells.core:
You meet each new piece of the work as it comes. You can tell what needs feeding from what needs leaving alone, and you give each one the size of care it can actually use. Two demands are calling at once and you're holding both without dropping either — not by force, by attention.

What you've already carried through has no more work in it, and you can let it go. Let the finish be a finish. When you hand over the account of what you gave — to the ones it was for, not to the record — the release turns into something closer to satisfaction than loss.
cells.sheetLine: You meet what arrives at the pace it can take, and you let what's finished be finished.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the threshold where what's arriving asks to be met

cells.tense: You're already standing in the harvest, bracing for an outcome you can't steer from here.
cells.ask: Name one thing whose ending you keep rehearsing, then do the small present act it's actually waiting for, and let the ending stay unwritten today.
cells.core:
Care that responds to what's here, a steady hand that doesn't exhaust itself, two needs held in balance — that ease is still in you. It's what makes the tending warm instead of grim.

What's taken its place is gripping. You're ahead of the thing you're tending, deciding when it should be done, checking it hasn't gone wrong, planning a harvest that hasn't ripened. The vigilance feels like real work and none of it reaches the plant. What loosens your hands is finishing something small and honest and letting the satisfaction of that arrive on its own time. Dream forward from what you've already carried through, not from what you're afraid of.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing a future you can't get to from here.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: at the threshold where what's arriving asks to be met

cells.tense: You set the work down some time back, and you're still standing where you left it.
cells.ask: Take up the smallest piece that was yours — one small tending, today — and let the strength come from doing it at all, not from doing it well.
cells.core:
When this is alive in what's arriving, you can name what the new thing needs, you go out and give it that, and the giving keeps its own warmth going. You knew how to do this. Nothing about the knowing has gone anywhere.

What's missing is the willingness to begin again without a guarantee. You can still see clearly what needs tending. You just aren't going out to it. Start with something small enough to finish. Keep reaching for one thing worth hoping about and the reaching itself will steady you. What you cultivate will get its own light back in time. Nothing here asks you to leap — it asks you to touch one thing that's still growing.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see what needs tending. You've stopped going out to it.

cells.tense: You're already carrying what's arriving — and you talk about it as if it arrived by itself.
cells.ask: Tell one person a concrete act of care you did this week as something you chose — once, plainly, without softening it.
cells.core:
Stewardship at its best here means someone meets the new work deliberately, decides what it's for, and holds it with a hand that knows its own strength. That deliberateness is running. It just hasn't been claimed.

The tending goes on quietly. You show up when no one asked, keep things alive that nobody is watching, carry what needs carrying — and you'd say none of that was you. You file it as upkeep, or as how things work. The decision is being made. It just hasn't been signed.

Take one thing you did out of care and stop calling it maintenance. The firmer your hand on what you actually chose, the less weight it costs to hold.
cells.sheetLine: You keep choosing the care. You keep calling it nothing.
